newsitem.title: UK: Emirates' Jan-May UK-Dubai cargo revenues up 49pct.
newsitem.headline: Emirates' Jan-May UK-Dubai cargo revenues up 49pct.

text.p: Emirates' ex-UK to Dubai air cargo revenues rose by 49 percent between January-May this year on the same period in 1996, said its UK cargo manager Ray Dissan.
He declined to give detailed figures but said this performance compared with a total market increase of 22 percent on the route during the five-month period.

"Despite the strength of the pound, the UAE is buying more and more British goods. There is a lot of loyalty to Britain in the UAE and Britain's message of delivering quality goods on time is getting through to UAE buyers," he told Reuters.
Dissan added that the Dubai government-owned airline has been able to cope with the extra demand due to a cargo capacity increase of 45 percent implemented on the UK-Dubai route last summer.

At that time, a schedule of 21 weekly Airbus A310/A300 services was replaced with 28 weekly flights on the route, 14 by new 25-tonne capacity Boeing 777s and 14 by a combination of the two Airbus types.
But Dissan warned that the growth of air cargo competition to Dubai was well exceeding local demand and potential.
He said that London, with a population of about 10 million, was served by 110 airlines. Dubai, with only 500,000 people, had 82 airlines regularly flying in and out.
"So proportionately, far more airlines are serving Dubai and the result is fierce competition and predatory pricing," he said.
"But that doesn't affect us. We go for the top end of the market and charge a premium for providing a high level of service. And our business keeps on growing," stated Dissan.
Turning to other ex-UK Middle Eastern air cargo markets, he made the following comments:
Abu Dhabi -- "It is a good market that showed healthy growth between January-May. Our revenues were up 60 percent during the period on the first five months of last year."
Doha -- "Again, a good, healthy market. From the UK, our business doubled in January-May."
Kuwait and Muscat -- "We have recently improved the frequency of our services to both destinations. Although has improved our market share, we have not dropped our prices."

Bahrain -- "As we have an open-skies policy, Gulf Air can and does fly into Dubai. But we are not allowed to serve Bahrain. As soon as we received the go-ahead, we would start straight away. But we see no breakthrough imminent."
Dissan said that no decision on any ex-UK cargo rate increases this winter had yet been taken,
"The strong pound has had some (detrimental) effect on our business, but the situation has not been as bad as a lot of British manufacturers feared," he noted.

"Nevertheless, cost inflation is still there and we would like to recoup some of this. But no adjustments would take place before our winter schedule comes into effect on November 1 and so we still have time before any rate rise decision is taken," he said. -Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Service; Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
